primary_reason: Official filings support a rapidly scaling AI-cloud business with contracted power, large customer commitments, and substantial liquidity, while the capital intensity and financing structure remain material constraints.
strongest_counter_case: The build-out requires unusually high capital deployment and external financing; customer concentration, accelerator supply, execution delays, dilution, secured debt, and regulatory or geopolitical constraints could impair cash generation before capacity produces durable returns.
invalidation_conditions: Official filings show a material loss, delay, or repricing of core contracted AI-cloud demand.
Verified liquidity and financing sources no longer cover the disclosed build-out path without materially adverse dilution or solvency risk.
Official evidence shows that power, site, or accelerator availability cannot support the announced capacity ramp.
next_research_triggers: Next official earnings release and filed financial statements.
New official financing, capacity, customer-concentration, or accelerator-supply disclosure.
A point-in-time issuer valuation packet using a validated completed-session market snapshot.

claims.normalized_claim: Nebius reports AI-cloud revenue expansion and a capital-intensive owned infrastructure build-out supported by contracted power.
An official filing discloses a multi-year infrastructure services framework with Meta and initial orders whose total value may reach approximately $27 billion.
The Q1 shareholder materials report substantial cash and positive operating cash flow, while later secured project financing shows continuing capital intensity and encumbrance risk.
Official filings disclose a pre-funded equity warrant and large convertible-note financing, creating dilution and financing-structure risk alongside liquidity.
Issuer operating evidence is available, but this slow baseline does not contain an approved point-in-time market-value packet; direct valuation therefore remains unverified.
